title: fix(collaboration,console): two more dates read the display locale, not the UI language (objectui#10375)
body:
Fixes #10375
Clause-②: no

Two more date faces take their locale from `useDisplayLocale()` instead of the UI language. Implemented by a dispatched dev subagent under seat `domain:ui#4` (session `session_01BP8CMtACxTdLjqR6rhd33C`), on base `74fcda829`.

## Premise, re-derived on `74fcda829`

Both sites were on `origin/main` as the card and the triage comment (`5823975048`) quote them:

- `ApprovalsInboxPage.tsx`, in `formatRelative`: `try { return new Date(s).toLocaleDateString(language); } catch { return s; }`, with `language` from `useObjectTranslation()`. The page already read `useDisplayLocale()` for every other date and number face.
- `CommentThread.tsx`: `formatAbsoluteDate(date, language)` ran `date.toLocaleDateString(language)`, with `language` from `useCollaborationTranslation()`, reached from `formatTimestamp` for comments seven or more days old.

A one-off probe that walks the census population exactly as `machineLocaleCensus-9909.test.ts` does (same manifests, same tooling filter, same comment masker, same matcher) finds exactly these two call sites passing a `language`-named first argument at `74fcda829`, and none at this branch's head.

## What changed

- `CommentThread` calls `useDisplayLocale()` in the component body, next to `useCollaborationTranslation()`, and passes the tag to `formatTimestamp` and on to `formatAbsoluteDate`. `language` had no other use there, so it is no longer destructured. The parameter is renamed `locale`, and the two doc comments now say the date follows the display locale and why objectui#3441 had chosen the session language. The inner `try/catch` for a malformed tag is unchanged.
- `ApprovalsInboxPage`: `formatRelative`'s date bucket passes the page's existing `displayLocale`, and the callback's dependency list names it instead of `language`. `language` had no other use in the page, so it is no longer destructured.
- Neither site adds a fallback. The hook owns the last-resort tag.
- The relative buckets ("just now", "5m ago", "3d ago") still go through `t` / `tr` and the UI language.
- `machineLocaleCensus-9909.test.ts`: the `CommentThread.tsx` DECLARED entry (the lit control) keeps its file, expression and count. The bare call in `formatAbsoluteDate`'s catch is still there, still counted once, and the lit-control case is green. Only its `reason` text changed, because its "whose `try` already passes the session language" would have gone false; it now names the display locale.
- Changeset: `patch` for `@object-ui/collaboration` and `@object-ui/console`. The dispatch named collaboration only; console is added because its source changes user-visibly too, and a changeset that describes the inbox without naming its package would leave the console changelog without the entry. The body states both behaviour changes.

## Mechanism readings (the dispatch's A1 to A4)

- **A1, no provider.** With no provider mounted, `useLocalization()` returns an empty object and `useDisplayLocale()` falls through to `useObjectTranslation().language`, the same tag `useCollaborationTranslation()` returned before. Measured with a new case in `comment-thread-no-provider-fallback.test.tsx`: every `toLocaleDateString` call receives exactly `'en'`, never the machine locale. The file's existing week-old-date case stays green. The file still does not import `@object-ui/i18n`; its docblock now says the tag is the display locale's fallthrough. Under an `I18nProvider` with no `LocalizationProvider`, the existing `zh` / `de` / `en_US` absolute-date cases in `comment-thread-i18n.test.tsx` stay green unchanged.
- **A2, relative buckets.** Both new pin files have a case where a three-day-old item under an English UI with a `de-CH` display locale reads `3d ago`. It stayed green on both ablation legs, as an invariance pin should.
- **A3, the pin.** See Tests and Ablation below.
- **A4, dependencies.** `@object-ui/collaboration` already depends on `@object-ui/i18n` (`workspace:*`), which exports `useDisplayLocale`. No dependency was added. The collaboration pins record the formatter argument with `vi.spyOn(Date.prototype, 'toLocaleDateString')` instead of `@object-ui/test-support`, which that package does not declare.

## Tests

New pins follow the objectui#10331 shape: the real `I18nProvider` with an English UI, and the display locale declared through `LocalizationProvider`, so the display locale is the only variable.

- `packages/collaboration/src/__tests__/comment-thread-display-locale-10375.test.tsx`: the `de-CH` pin (`4.3.2020`, and equal to the runtime's own `de-CH` rendering), the `en-US` control (`3/4/2020`), a differential no runner locale can satisfy, an argument check (every `toLocaleDateString` call received `de-CH`), the relative-bucket invariance case, and a malformed display locale (`de_CH`) that still falls back to the runtime date, never the raw ISO string.
- `apps/console/src/pages/system/ApprovalsInboxPage.displayLocale-10375.test.tsx`: the same pin, control, differential and relative-bucket cases, read from the queue cell whose `title` tooltip is the (untouched) `formatDate` face, plus the `@object-ui/test-support` tripwire. `consoleFaces.displayLocale-9909.test.tsx` could not see this defect: it stubs the UI language to `'en'` and its tripwire tolerates any declared tag, so only the machine locale reads as red there.

Runs from the repo root at `5a40f03e0`, through the shared verify lock:

- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/collaboration/ apps/console/src/pages/system/ apps/console/src/pages/consoleFaces.displayLocale-9909.test.tsx apps/console/src/__tests__/approvalsInboxComponentRef.test.tsx packages/app-shell/src/views/__tests__/DeclaredActionsBar.test.tsx packages/i18n/src/__tests__/dead-pack-keys-retired-8754.test.ts packages/i18n/src/__tests__/machineLocaleCensus-9909.test.ts` gives `Test Files 30 passed (30)` and `Tests 264 passed (264)`. That covers both new pins, every collaboration suite, every approvals-inbox suite, the other suites that name `ApprovalsInboxPage`, and the census.
- Type-check after the closure builds: `turbo run build --filter="@object-ui/collaboration^..."` (3 of 3 tasks), then `pnpm --filter @object-ui/collaboration run type-check` and `pnpm --filter @object-ui/i18n run type-check`, both exit 0. `turbo run build --filter="@object-ui/console^..."` (34 of 34 tasks), then the console's `type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -b tsconfig.node.json --force`) exits 0. `--listFiles` shows the programs contain the new files: 6 collaboration test files in its `tsconfig.test.json`, the census file in i18n's, and both the page and the new pin in the console program (its `include` is `src`).

## Ablation: fix committed first, every leg restored with on-disk proof

Each leg puts the UI language back at ONE face through `ablation-replace.mjs`, then runs both pin files and the no-provider file (27 cases).

| leg | mutation | red | green |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| CommentThread | `const displayLocale = useDisplayLocale();` becomes `const displayLocale = useCollaborationTranslation().language;` | that face's de-CH pin, differential and argument check (3) | its en-US control, relative bucket and malformed-tag case, the no-provider file and the inbox pins (24) |
| ApprovalsInboxPage | `const { t } = useObjectTranslation();` becomes `const { t, language } = useObjectTranslation();` (held), then `toLocaleDateString(displayLocale); } catch { return s; }` becomes `toLocaleDateString(language); } catch { return s; }` | that face's de-CH pin, differential and tripwire (3) | 24 |

The red readings:

- CommentThread: `got: 3/4/2020: expected '3/4/2020' to be '4.3.2020'`, and the argument check `saw: [["en"]]`.
- ApprovalsInboxPage: `got: 3/4/2020: expected '3/4/2020' to be '4.3.2020'`, and the tripwire saw four `Date.prototype.toLocaleDateString` calls, each with `"locale":"en"`.

The malformed-tag case stays green on the CommentThread leg. It pins the catch fallback, not the channel, so it is not offered as evidence for this change.

On-disk proof:

- CommentThread: anchor 1 to 0, blob `b3733ea1a9cf` to `d73d4e95d0e6`, restored to `b3733ea1a9cf` (HEAD's), `git diff HEAD` empty.
- ApprovalsInboxPage: the held leg moved the blob `7869008b0099` to `d086337684fc`, and the wrapped leg moved it on to `f334af56992a`. The wrapped leg's restore took the whole file back to HEAD, so both mutations were gone after it (on-disk counts 0 and 0), blob `7869008b0099`, `git diff HEAD` empty.
- A shell trap restored both paths from HEAD with absolute paths, and `git status --porcelain` was empty at the end.

No `dist/` is on the path: the pins import the components by relative path, and vitest aliases `@object-ui/i18n`, `@object-ui/collaboration` and `@object-ui/test-support` to `src`.

## Gates

`dispatch-gates.mjs` only works in objectstack, so these were derived by hand from this repo's `package.json` and `.github/workflows/`. All at `5a40f03e0`, all exit 0:

- `check-changeset-presence`: 6 source files of 3 released packages changed, 1 changeset declared.
- `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-overwrite` (1 added, 0 modified), `check-changeset-fixed`.
- `check-changeset-claims`: no line address in this change's own prose; no self-contradiction. The went-false reading names two pending changesets that mention `machineLocaleCensus-9909.test.ts`: `9786-detail-timestamps-display-locale.md` and `9909-machine-locale-sweep.md`. I read both paragraphs. They say collaboration's single hit is a deliberate catch fallback for a tag `Intl` rejected, and describe what the census refuses. Both still hold.
- `check:new-line-citations`: `VERDICT new-cross-file-line-citations: 0 new citation(s)`. `check:control-bytes`: OK.
- For the new tests: `check-vi-mock-specifiers`, `check-vi-mock-inherit`, `check-vi-mock-override-shape`, `check-test-path-roots`, `check-pending-changeset-literals`. For the source: `check-phantom-dependencies`, `check-unused-dependencies`, `check-package-self-import`, `check-unreferenced-sources`, `check-i18n-call-site-keys`.
- Lint: the full `pnpm lint` is left to CI. ESLint with `--no-inline-config` ran on the 6 changed TS files (each package's `lint` is `eslint .` over the root config).
  - Result: 6 files, 0 errors. The four test files have no warnings. `ApprovalsInboxPage.tsx` has 20 warnings and `CommentThread.tsx` has 1, with the same per-rule counts as their base blobs.
  - `eslint --print-config` resolves all 6 files, so none of them is ignored.
  - `eslint.config.js` configures no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService`). So this diff cannot change the lint result of a file it does not touch.

## The census extension to a bare `language` argument: not built here

The card says objectui#10369's PR body costs this extension as cheap. That body says the opposite: "Not cheap: a bare `language` argument (the UI-language channel) cannot be told apart from a correctly named variable without data flow", and adds that such a rule would land red on three sites. The dispatch allowed the extension only if it is as cheap as that costing says, so it is not built. The conflict is reported to the seat.

Measured here for whoever prices the follow-up: the "lands red" half no longer holds. The probe described above finds the two sites this PR changes at `74fcda829` and none at head. Among the census population's identifier first arguments at head, the last segments are `locale`, `displayLocale`, `dateLocale`, `effectiveLocale` and one constant, and none is `language`. The data-flow half still holds: a name rule would judge the identifier, not where its value came from.

## Acceptance notes

- `formatRelative`'s catch (like `formatDate`'s) returns the raw value when `Intl` rejects the tag. A malformed display locale would therefore show the raw ISO string in the inbox, where `CommentThread` falls back to the runtime date. This PR does not make that more likely: the old `language` argument had the same exposure. No malformed tenant locale was reproduced, so nothing was filed.
- No README or `content/docs` change: neither `@object-ui/collaboration`'s README nor the docs describe how the timestamp is formatted. The changeset carries the user-facing sentence.
